description: Agent Mining Records: submit mine permit records as issued with the mine record and the production and tailings entries they answer to: the mine with its reference, name and the permit numbers it claims; each permit with its id, reference (the permit number), issuer, the mine it is issued to and the moments issued and expiring; each permit condition with its id, reference, the permit, what it limits (production or tailings), the maximum it allows and the moments its period starts and ends; each mining production entry with its id, reference, the permit, the tonnage and the production day; each tailings deposition entry with its id, reference, the permit, the amount and the moment deposited. The signed report gives the permits and the records behind them, each permit the mine record claims against the permits as issued, each permit against the mine it is issued to, each production entry against the expiry of its permit, and each condition against the production or tailings entries under its permit in its period, and counts them, and names divergent mine permit records: a permit the mine record claims that the permit record does not show, a permit issued to a mine other than the one the mine record identifies, production recorded under a permit already expired on its date, and production or tailings entries past a permit condition’s limit; then a permit entry missing its issuer or expiry date and a production or tailings entry naming a permit the record does not show, with the fix for each and what would change the verdict. No permit entries, or no production entries beside a production condition, leaves those points unverified. Permits, mines and entries match by letters and digits, tonnage and amounts to the hundredth, dates and periods by the day, a permit is current through the day it expires, and an entry equal to a condition’s limit is inside it. This reads the mine’s own permits as issued: wever_build-permit-check reads a building permit filing against the plans and inspections, while the mine permit record check reads mine permits against the mine’s production and tailings. Verdict mine_permit_record_divergent, mine_permit_record_partial, mine_permit_record_unverified or mine_permit_record_consistent. POST /api/mining-permit-record-check. Reads the mining records supplied in the call and returns a signed report with the verdict, the evidence read, the findings with their fixes, and what would change the verdict; it reads the records as supplied only: it operates no mine, contacts no regulator, land office or other operator and issues no permit, claim or certification, which stay with the mine operator, the land office and the regulators, and the records stay in the report, with no network request, fetch, message, payment or external write. Agent Mining Records reads mineral extraction records (hard-rock, coal, aggregate and quarry operations), not cryptocurrency mining and not data mining; the Agent Datasets family reads data sets. It reads a mine operator’s own records: mine records with operator licensing and certification entries, mining claim records for mineral land, mine permit records as issued, mine inspection records with citations and abatements, mine safety records with the blasting log, mining production records by period, the mine’s own tailings facility records and reclamation records with their bond entries, each against the permit, claim, production, certification, schedule, corrective action, shipment, capacity, closure and bond records it answers to. The family’s ground is the mine’s paper trail: what the mine record claims, whether the claims, permits and inspections hold up, what the safety and production records support, and whether the tailings and reclamation records line up; it reads by record holder and subject: the Agent Agriculture Records family reads a farm’s production and land records, the Agent Waste and Recycling Records family reads manifested waste and disposal records, wever_water-discharge-record-check reads mine effluent monitoring, and the Agent Claims family reads insurance claims, while this family reads the mine’s own records and reads none of those. Paid URL: 0.10 USDC per call on Base via x402 exact, with the shared 10 signed-wallet free calls per rolling 30 days. Bind X-Wever-Wallet-Proof to the exact JSON arguments and the tool route. Returns a report with an Ed25519 signed receipt. Contract: /api/agent-mining-records-contract. Human page: https://weverlabs.com/agent-mining-records/.

conditions.description: Each permit condition with a stated limit.

from.description: When the condition period starts, such as 2026-03-02.

kind.description: What the condition limits: production or tailings.

maximum.description: Amount the condition allows, in the unit the record uses.

to.description: When the condition period ends, such as 2026-03-02.

label.description: Optional name recorded in the report.

permits.description: Permit numbers the mine record claims.
Each permit as issued in the mine permit record.

expires_at.description: When the permit expires, such as 2026-03-02.

mine.description: The mine the permit is issued to reference.

tonnage.description: Amount produced, in the unit the record uses.

amount.description: Amount deposited, in the unit the record uses.
